draft.title: Models of the atom over time
card: Dalton
Dalton pictured atoms as tiny solid balls, with no parts inside. Each element had its own kind of ball.
Thomson
Thomson found electrons, which are tiny negative particles inside atoms. So atoms were not solid balls with nothing inside.
Rutherford
Rutherford fired particles at thin gold foil. Most passed straight through, but a few bounced back. This showed a tiny, dense nucleus with protons, and mostly empty space around it.
Later models
Bohr placed electrons in shells around the nucleus. Chadwick then found neutrons, which sit in the nucleus with the protons.
draft.remember: Each new model was built from new evidence, from a solid ball to a nucleus with electrons in shells.

a.q: In Rutherford's gold foil test, a few particles bounced back. What did this show about the atom?
opts: It has a tiny, dense nucleus
It is a solid ball of matter
It has electrons in shells only
It has no particles inside it
a.why: Only a very small, dense centre could bounce particles straight back, while most passed through empty space. A solid ball would have stopped or deflected most of the particles, so that model did not fit the result.
a.clue: What could be small enough to hit only a few particles?

b.q: A teacher says Dalton's model was replaced after electrons were found. Why was it replaced?
opts: Atoms were shown to have smaller parts inside
Atoms were shown to be much larger than thought
Atoms were shown to have no mass at all
Atoms were shown to be made of only neutrons
b.why: Finding electrons showed that atoms have parts inside, which a solid ball with no parts could not explain. Size and mass were not what changed the model, and neutrons were found later.
b.clue: Dalton's atoms had no parts inside.

a.best: It has a tiny, dense nucleus

b.best: Atoms were shown to have smaller parts inside

problems.detail: Why (a) says a solid ball would have stopped or deflected most of the particles. Historically, the model being tested was Thomson's, which predicted that almost all particles would pass through with only small deflections. The surprise was that a few bounced back. Contrasting the result with a solid ball misstates what the experiment ruled out.

proposal.title: Models of the atom over time
card: Dalton
Dalton pictured atoms as tiny solid balls, with no parts inside. Each element had its own kind of ball.
Thomson
Thomson found electrons, which are tiny negative particles inside atoms. He pictured them spread through a ball of positive charge.
Rutherford

Rutherford fired positive particles at thin gold foil. Thomson's model predicted they would all pass through with only small bends, but a few bounced back. This showed a tiny, dense, positive nucleus with mostly empty space around it.
Later models
Bohr placed electrons in shells around the nucleus. Protons were found in the nucleus, and Chadwick later found neutrons there too.
proposal.remember: Each new model was built from new evidence, from a solid ball to a nucleus with electrons in shells.

a.q: In Rutherford's gold foil test, a few particles bounced back. What did this show about the atom?
opts: Its positive charge is packed in a tiny centre
Its positive charge is spread right through it
It is a solid ball with no parts inside
Its electrons sit in shells around it
a.why: In Thomson's model the positive charge was spread out, so the particles should all have passed through with only small bends. A few bouncing back meant the positive charge and mass were packed into a tiny, dense nucleus, with mostly empty space around it.
a.clue: Thomson's model predicted that nothing would bounce back.
